subject: AI & Agents
title: Layers: Building Depth
description: A short lesson to help you apply Layers: Building Depth.

hook.text: Layer 1 detects edges. Layer 2 detects shapes. Layer 3 detects objects. Depth creates abstraction.

buildup.text: Neural networks stack layers. Each layer transforms its input into a more abstract representation.

discovery.text: Early layers learn simple features. Deeper layers combine them into complex concepts.

twist.text: Too few layers and the network can't learn. Too many and it becomes hard to train.

climax.text: GPT-4 has over 100 layers. Each one refines the representation of your text.

punchline.text: Intelligence is abstraction, and abstraction needs depth.

quiz.question: What happens as you go deeper in a neural network?
options: Features become more abstract and complex

details.summary: Neural networks stack layers of neurons, each transforming its input. Depth allows networks to learn hierarchical representations — from raw pixels to edges to shapes to complete objects across successive layers.
details.whyItMatters: Depth is what makes deep learning deep. More layers enable the model to discover increasingly abstract patterns. Understanding layers reveals how AI builds complex understanding from simple elements.
takeaways: Layers progressively transform data into abstract representations
More layers enable detection of more complex patterns
Depth is the key difference between shallow and deep learning

faq.question: How many layers does a typical neural network have?
faq.answer: It varies widely. Simple classifiers may have 3-5 layers. Image recognition networks like ResNet have 50-152. Large language models have 80-120 transformer layers. Depth depends on task complexity.

faq.question: Can adding more layers always improve performance?
faq.answer: Not always. Very deep networks suffer from vanishing gradients and diminishing returns. Techniques like skip connections help, but eventually adding depth increases cost without meaningful accuracy gains.
